Batch: 2023, 7th Semester Academic Year: 2026-27 Semester Duration: 27th July to 20th November 2026 Course Faculty: Dr. Soharab Hossain Shaikh Email: soharab.hossain@bmu.edu.in Office: E2 Building, 4th Floor, Cabin No. 81 Mr. Pranshu Tiwari Email: v-pranshu.tiwari@bmu.edu.in Course Coordinator Dr. Soharab Hossain Shaikh Aim of the Course: The course aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills needed to design, build, and deploy intelligent multi-agent workflows powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). Students will learn to harness the reasoning capabilities of LLMs to automate complex, context-aware tasks

needed to design, build, and deploy intelligent multi-agent workflows powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). Students will learn to harness the reasoning capabilities of LLMs to automate complex, context-aware tasks using advanced agentic design patterns. Emphasis is placed on real-world application, secure deployment, and data privacy, including the use of local LLMs. By the end of the course, students will be prepared to develop robust, scalable AI-driven task automation systems across diverse domains. Course Overview and Context: "Agentic AI" is an advanced undergraduate course designed to explore the intersection of artificial intelligence, natural language processing, and task automation. The course spans over 16 weeks and provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to build intelligent multi- agent systems

artificial intelligence, natural language processing, and task automation. The course spans over 16 weeks and provides learners with the knowledge and practical skills required to build intelligent multi- agent systems powered by Large Language Models (LLMs). Emphasizing task automation through structured conversational workflows, the course begins with the review of foundational concepts such as transformer architecture, embeddings, LLM training, etc. Further, learners will explore agentic design patterns - including planning, reasoning, tool use, and self-reflection - and gain hands-on experience with leading frameworks such as CrewAI and Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK). The course also covers emerging communication protocols like Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Google’s Agent2Agent (A2A), with a strong focus on secure, responsible deployment using monitoring, observability,

The course also covers emerging communication protocols like Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Google’s Agent2Agent (A2A), with a strong focus on secure, responsible deployment using monitoring, observability, and guardrails. By the end of the course, participants will be able to design and deploy multi-modal agents across domains such as customer support, healthcare, and automated software development. Course Philosophy: This course will be delivered using a Project-Based Learning (PjBL) approach, where students learn Agentic AI related concepts by designing and developing AI agents to solve complex real-world problems. CS301 - Operating Systems Course Handout / Syllabus Unit 1: Introduction to Operating Systems - What is an operating system, goals and functions - Types of operating systems: batch, multiprogrammed, time-sharing, distributed, real-time - System calls and system programs overview Unit 2: Process Management - Process concept, process states, process control block - Process scheduling queues and schedulers - CPU scheduling: First Come First Serve (FCFS), Shortest Job First (SJF), Round Robin - Brief comparison of scheduling algorithms using turnaround time and waiting time Unit 3: Process Synchronization - Critical section problem, Peterson's solution - Semaphores: definition and usage (introductory treatment only, one lecture) - Classical synchronization problems mentioned by name only: producer-consumer, readers-writers Unit 4: Memory Management - Contiguous

section problem, Peterson's solution - Semaphores: definition and usage (introductory treatment only, one lecture) - Classical synchronization problems mentioned by name only: producer-consumer, readers-writers Unit 4: Memory Management - Contiguous memory allocation, fragmentation - Paging: basic concept, page tables - Segmentation: basic concept - Virtual memory overview, demand paging Unit 5: File Systems and Storage - File concepts, directory structure - File allocation methods: contiguous, linked, indexed - Disk structure overview Unit 6: Miscellaneous Topics - Deadlocks: definition and the four necessary conditions (single slide, not covered in depth) - Protection and security: brief overview Note: Disk scheduling algorithms (SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK) and deadlock avoidance algorithms (Banker's Algorithm) are NOT covered in lecture slides this semester due to time constraints;

Protection and security: brief overview Note: Disk scheduling algorithms (SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK) and deadlock avoidance algorithms (Banker's Algorithm) are NOT covered in lecture slides this semester due to time constraints; students are pointed to the textbook chapter for self-study only. Recommended Textbook: Silberschatz, Galvin, Gagne - Operating System Concepts
